_comment: Third-party data connectors, wired natively via OpenClaw MCP servers.
Copy to config/connectors.json (gitignored, not in the release manifest) and edit.
render_channel_config.py injects each enabled entry as mcp.servers.<name> in the
rendered runtime config and appends the <name>__* glob to each listed specialist's
own agents.list[].tools.allow. That per-agent list is the only tool layer the
renderer touches: the fixed tools.subagents.tools.allow in config/openclaw.json is
left as shipped, and the grantable specialists (render_channel_config.py
CONNECTOR_GRANTABLE_AGENTS) run as subagents of vc-chief, not as top-level
agents. Whether that layer also has to name a dynamic MCP tool id was never
measured, so commissioning must prove the specialist can call the tool, not only
that the server answers: after openclaw mcp doctor <name> --probe passes, invoke
one connector tool from a granting specialist and keep the result with the
commissioning record. Put API keys in the gateway environment and
reference them as ${VAR}; secrets are never written into this file or the config.
OpenClaw ships no Crunchbase/PitchBook server: point at a hosted third-party
MCP server URL or a thin MCP shim over the vendor's REST API. A stdio/npx
server cannot run in the shipped gateway container (read-only filesystem, no
registry access): baking its package into the derived image is a reviewed
commissioning change (runtime-packages pin, rebuild, G6).
Live connectivity is a deployment-commissioning check, not a package guarantee,
and the bar is the two steps above -- probe, then one real connector tool call
from a granting specialist -- not the probe alone. The config surface is what
this release provides; see workspaces/vc-chief/vc/third_party_connectors.md.
